text:
michelle: heads up — Nimbus reported a sudden p99 jump on their /complete endpoint starting ~2024-11-03 14:12 UTC. They're on Dedicated in us-west-2. Saw ~3x p99 increase, p50 stable. sharing traces now.
support-bot: new escalation created: INC-9876. Customer: Nimbus. Link: https://support.example.com/tickets/INC-9876 :rotating_light:
raj: can you paste the trace ids / span ids so i can correlate with traces?
michelle: trace ids: 8f1a2b4c...ef90 (short). logs show a handful of requeues at worker level around the requests. cpu looks fine, gpu util up ~10%. attaching perf snippet: ```
[2024-11-03T14:12:22Z] request=tx_8f1a2b4c latency=2100ms stage=batcher size=56
[2024-11-03T14:12:22Z] request=tx_8f1a2b4c event=requeue reason=kv_miss
[2024-11-03T14:12:23Z] request=tx_9a2b3c4d latency=87ms stage=kernel
```
tanya: requeues often point to a KV cache miss storm or batching delays. which kernel-selector and batching policy are they on?
michelle: selector v2.3.1, batcher policy = autoscale-burst (changed last week). batching window 10ms, max_batch=64. KV TTL 30s.
sam: can someone reproduce with a synthetic load that matches their QPS + token distribution? what's the target profile?
michelle: their sustained QPS ~120 req/s, median input length ~1024 tokens, gen length ~8 tokens. Need to reproduce p99 spikes. can someone run rbench using nimbus_profile.json for 5m.
liam: i'm free, will run it on bench-host-12. where's the profile file?
michelle: uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-bench/profiles/nimbus_profile.json (internal). note: include KV miss pattern in workload.
liam: kicking off: ```rbench run --model redwood-v1-large --batcher auto --workload /tmp/nimbus_profile.json --duration 300 --trace-collect```
liam: first pass shows p99 ~2.1s, matches customer. enabling kernel selector debug: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` to capture decisions.
tanya: also try `--batcher fixed --batch-size 32` to see if big batches are causing tail.
liam: good idea. running fixed batch_size=32 now.
liam: fixed(32) p99 ~1.1s. so autoscale-burst/auto batching sometimes produces very large batches that push latency at the tail.
michelle: interesting — autoscale-burst was rolled last tuesday for higher throughput. who changed tenant config?
raj: that was me, rolled throughput config to allow burst batching for higher throughput for a few tenants. i can revert for Nimbus if needed.
sam: before a revert, can we check cache hitrates? could be combined effect: cache miss storm + large batches.
liam: bench run shows KV cache hitrate baseline 98% but drops to ~70% during spike windows. reproduces locally. so two factors: cache-dip causes more work per request and large batches amplify p99.
michelle: ok action list: 1) @raj revert burst-batching for Nimbus tenant as a short-term mitigation 2) @sam + @liam draft per-tenant batcher pinning + KV prewarm recommendations 3) support to notify customer of mitigation and ETA. owners?
raj: reverting now to previous batcher policy for nimbus-tenant group. ETA ~2m.
ops-bot: deploy started: config/nimbus-tenant/batcher -> revert (deploy id dpl-3345).
raj: revert completed. monitoring for impact.
liam: re-ran bench after revert: p99 dropped to ~1.05s. KV hit dip still happens but less amplification.
sam: i'll draft a runbook + template for tenant-specific `batcher: fixed` overrides and a section on KV prewarm (increase TTL on hotspots, issue background warmup queries).
michelle: support, please send a short note to customer: "We identified a combination of transient KV cache misses and a recent 'burst' batching policy causing intermittent tail latency. We've rolled back the batching change for your tenant and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a permanent fix and recommendations."
support-bot: message queued to customer via ticket INC-9876.
michelle: nice work. i'll open a follow-up PR to add a per-tenant batcher flag + an alert that fires when KV hitrate drops >15% within 1m.
tanya: add an eval that tracks p99 vs batch size and suggests batcher mode in Console. could be an auto-suggestion.
michelle: yep — i'll include that in the PR. thanks all. closing loop for now — we'll sync async on the runbook/PR. :white_check_mark:
